Much of it is personal preference; however, one of the reasons why many people don't prefer short hair cuts is purely due to how the brain evaluates one as being of good stock (both men and women's brains do this).

The reason we find people physically attractive is because the brain, without conscious intent, evaluates everyone in order to determine if that person has good genes and would be a suitable mate. It's weird, but that's what happens. If someone is attractive, it is the brains way to expressing the outcome of that evaluation. For example, someone who is obese is not seen as being good for bearing or raising children. This is expressed by the brain as seeing that other person as "ugly" or unattractive. It's a pretty neat how the brain actually does with without us knowing. Of course, this is only for physical, appearance related, stuff (like a haircut). The brain actually has been shown to follow what is called the golden ratio on others faces in determining attraction. In short, the more a persons facial structure conforms to the golden ratio, the more "attractive," they appear to anyone.

All of this explanation comes down to this. Long hair is a sign of good genetics. You may be able to grow long and wavy hair, but just choose to cut it short; regardless, the brain usually doesn't see short hair as being a sign of good genetics. Long and healthy hair is usually seen by the brain as a good trait in a mate, so it's seen as being more attractive to some people.

But, of course, some people do prefer shorter hair, though most people do actually like longer hair. Just a more biological explanation to why some don't like shorter hair.
